sup.getting_started_sub: Set up WristVox in under 2 minutes.
sup.step1.title: Install WristVox on your Mac
sup.step1.desc: Download WristVox for Mac from wristvox.app and drag it to your Applications folder. Launch the app — it lives in your menu bar.
sup.step2.title: Grant permissions
sup.step2.desc: WristVox needs two permissions: Accessibility (to send keystrokes like Fn key double-tap for dictation) and Dictation enabled in System Settings. The onboarding wizard will guide you through both.
sup.step3.title: Get WristVox on your Apple Watch or iPhone
sup.step3.desc: Download WristVox from the App Store on your iPhone — the Watch app installs automatically. Both iPhone and Watch work as remotes.
sup.step4.title: Pair with a code and start dictating
sup.step4.desc: Open WristVox on your Watch or iPhone — it will find your Mac via Bluetooth. Confirm the 4-digit pairing code shown on your Mac, and you're connected. Tap Dictate — your Mac starts listening. Speak, then tap Send.
sup.faq1.q: How do I grant Accessibility permission on macOS?
sup.faq1.a: Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, then toggle WristVox on. If WristVox is not listed, click the "+" button and add it from your Applications folder. You may need to unlock the settings by clicking the lock icon first.
sup.faq2.q: My Watch doesn't see the Mac — what should I do?
sup.faq2.a: Make sure Bluetooth is enabled on both devices and WristVox is running on your Mac. On your Watch, open WristVox and wait a few seconds — the first connection can take 5–10 seconds. If it still doesn't connect, try toggling Bluetooth off and on again on the Mac.
sup.faq3.q: Dictation doesn't start when I tap the button.
sup.faq3.a: WristVox activates dictation by simulating a double-tap of the Fn key (Fn×2), which is the standard macOS shortcut. Make sure Dictation is enabled: System Settings → Keyboard → Dictation → toggle On. Also verify that Accessibility permission is granted for WristVox.
sup.faq4.q: I have to re-grant Accessibility after every app update.
sup.faq4.a: This is a macOS security requirement. When the app binary changes after an update, macOS may revoke its Accessibility access. You'll need to re-enable it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
sup.faq5.q: Does WristVox work with non-English keyboard layouts?
sup.faq5.a: Yes! WristVox uses a layout-independent method to activate dictation (Fn key double-tap), which works reliably across all keyboard layouts and input methods.
sup.faq6.a: No. WristVox has no servers, no accounts, no analytics, and no tracking. Everything works over a direct Bluetooth connection between your Watch and your Mac. Nothing ever leaves your devices.
sup.known_issues_sub: Issues we're aware of and actively working on.
sup.issue1.title: Accessibility permission resets after app update
sup.issue1.desc: macOS revokes Accessibility access when the app binary changes. You need to re-enable it in System Settings after each update.
sup.issue2.title: First BLE connection may take 5–10 seconds
sup.issue2.desc: The initial Bluetooth connection after launching the app requires a radio warmup period. Subsequent reconnections are faster.

priv.title: Privacy Policy
priv.tldr: WristVox doesn't collect any data about you. All communication happens locally via Bluetooth between your Apple Watch and your Mac. No servers, no accounts, no analytics, no tracking. Your privacy is fully protected.
priv.collection_bold: We do not collect any personal data.
priv.collection: WristVox operates entirely on your local devices and does not collect personal information, track usage or analytics, send data to remote servers, use third-party analytics services, store data in the cloud, or require account creation.
priv.how1: WristVox uses Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) to communicate between your Apple Watch, iPhone, and Mac. This communication happens entirely locally between your devices, does not pass through any servers, is not monitored or logged, and contains only simple command signals.
priv.how2: WristVox does not require an internet connection to function. All features work completely offline.
priv.perms_bt: Bluetooth — to receive commands from your Apple Watch and iPhone. Limited to local device communication.
priv.perms_ax: Accessibility — to trigger keyboard shortcuts and mouse actions on your Mac. WristVox does not read, access, or store any data from other applications.
priv.perms_mobile_bt: Bluetooth — to send commands to your Mac. Limited to local device communication. Only sends simple command signals.
priv.third: WristVox does not use any third-party services, including analytics providers, crash reporting services, advertising networks, cloud storage providers, or social media integrations.
priv.storage: All app settings and preferences are stored locally on your devices using standard Apple frameworks (UserDefaults). No data is synced to the cloud.
priv.children: WristVox does not collect any data from anyone, including children under 13. The app is rated 4+ and contains no age-inappropriate content.
priv.rights: Since we don't collect any data, there is no personal data to request access to, request deletion of, request correction of, or export. You maintain complete control over your data at all times.
priv.changes: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. If we make material changes, we will update the effective date above and publish a new version on our website.
